applicability.reason: Harness has complete Android/Binder/model lifecycle workflows whose assembled outcome is not fully established by unit and host contract tests alone.

target_environments.description: Representative physical Android ARM64 device running the Harness app, native llama.cpp backend and real GGUF model artifacts.
material_dimensions: arm64-v8a ABI and JNI/native llama.cpp backend
real GGUF storage and model lifecycle
Binder/process behavior where shared-runtime surfaces are exercised

does not load a production GGUF through the llama.cpp backend
does not establish physical memory, thermal or OEM behavior
Binder Parcelable evidence is narrower than a full two-application host/client round trip

execution_environments.platform: GitHub-hosted Linux + Android API 35 Google APIs x86_64 emulator
execution_environments.artifact_surface: installed phone debug APK derived from the production-shaped ARM64 debug APK by removing native library entries and re-signing only for the no-native cold-start canary
known_gaps: the canary intentionally removes the ARM64 native payload and therefore does not prove native loading or inference
the re-signed canary is not the release/promoted artifact and does not establish production signing identity
x86_64 emulator does not represent ARM64 package installation, physical memory, thermal or OEM behavior
the journey proves clean startup remains independent of JNI; native packaging/linkability remains covered separately

execution_environments.artifact_surface: installed Harness debug/release-candidate app plus identity-bearing device evidence scripts
known_gaps: one representative device does not establish every supported OEM/device configuration

critical_journeys.claim: The public Android Binder contract types survive Android framework parceling/unparceling with the expected contract semantics.
residual_gaps: full cross-process/two-application service lifecycle remains a stronger journey than Parcelable contract evidence

critical_journeys.claim: A clean Harness process can install and render the initial phone shell without loading or requiring the native llama.cpp/JNI payload during application startup.
residual_gaps: the no-native canary does not prove ARM64 native linker compatibility, model loading or inference
release signing and exact promoted-artifact launch remain separate packaging/physical evidence

critical_journeys.claim: A verified compatible GGUF can be selected, prepared, streamed/cancelled through the production native backend, and cleaned up with truthful lifecycle/resource evidence on Android ARM64.
residual_gaps: real model loading and memory reclamation
critical_journeys.automation_gap_reason: Current hosted CI has no representative Android ARM64 device/model environment for the production llama.cpp backend. Lower-level deterministic tests cover orchestration and contracts, while identity-bearing physical-device evidence owns the remaining native/model/resource claim.
